sources.title: Surge of neurophysiological coupling and connectivity of gamma oscillations in the dying human brain
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
limitations: Observational analysis of four comatose dying patients after withdrawal of ventilatory support.
Gamma surges occurred in two patients and are not direct reports of conscious experience.
Neural signatures associated with conscious processing are not proof of consciousness or post-mortem survival.

sources.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
limitations: Tests selected predictions of IIT and GNWT under conscious visual-perception conditions.
Challenges to theory predictions do not establish that either theory is wholly false.
The study does not test consciousness after irreversible biological death.

sources.title: Guidelines and standards for the study of death and recalled experiences of death—a multidisciplinary consensus statement and proposed future directions
sources.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
limitations: Consensus and methodological proposal rather than a prospective empirical test.
Terminology and interpretations in this paper are contested in the literature.
Must be presented alongside the existing Martial et al. 2022 methodological critique.
Consensus language does not prove survival or non-survival.

claims.text: In an observational analysis of four comatose dying patients, two exhibited surges of gamma power, cross-frequency coupling and connectivity after withdrawal of ventilatory support.
limitations: Small observational sample; neural activity is not a direct measure or report of experience.
claims.uncertainty: The findings show that selected neurophysiological activity can occur during the dying process but do not establish consciousness or post-mortem continuation.
provenance: peer-reviewed primary observational study and indexed bibliographic record

claims.text: A preregistered adversarial collaboration found results that challenged specific predictions of both integrated information theory and global neuronal workspace theory.
limitations: The experiments addressed selected theory predictions in visual consciousness, not every claim of either theory.
claims.uncertainty: The results constrain theory development but do not resolve the ontology of consciousness or survival after death.
provenance: peer-reviewed preregistered adversarial collaboration and publisher version of record

claims.text: A multidisciplinary group proposed terminology and methodological standards for studying death and recalled experiences associated with cardiac arrest and other life-threatening events.
limitations: Consensus terminology is a proposal and has received peer-reviewed methodological criticism.
claims.uncertainty: The proposal may improve standardisation but does not determine the timing, mechanism or ontology of reported experiences.
provenance: peer-reviewed consensus/methods paper paired with existing peer-reviewed methodological critique

batch_conclusion.statement: The three candidates add observations and methodological context relevant to dying-brain neurophysiology and theories of consciousness. They do not establish conscious experience during irreversible brain failure, post-mortem continuity, or its impossibility.
